**Triage: lands in `packages/cli` (`os validate` / `os lint` wiring of the ADR-0130 D4 union fold); `domain:cli`; `priority:p1`.**

A project whose definitions live **only in `packages[]`** — the ADR-0130 D4 artifact shape — is judged by `os validate` and `os lint` as if it declared **nothing**. Both **exit 0 with no diagnostic of any severity**. `os build` judges the same stack correctly and **exits 1**.

⇒ ⭐ **Two of the three authoring gates report a clean bill of health on a stack they read nothing of.** That is why this is p1 rather than p2: it is not a gate that misses a case, it is a gate that **certifies an unread project as clean**, and it does so silently at exit 0. An author running `os validate` before shipping gets the strongest possible false assurance.

⇒ Wire `authoringRuleUnionStack` (the ADR-0130 D4 fold) into `os validate` and `os lint`, as it already is in `os build`. ⇒ the shape is settled — `os build` is the working reference.

⚠️ **Expect previously-silent projects to start failing.** That is the defect surfacing; ⛔ do not soften the new diagnostics to keep exit codes stable. ⚠️ But **do** say in the PR what the in-repo examples do once the gates actually read them — if the platform's own examples go red, that is a second finding and needs its own card, ⛔ not a quiet fix here.

⭐ The card names the class correctly: this is the *"weakest gate"* shape — three gates, one honest.

⚠️ **Reported to the maintainer in this round's report** as a false-green at an authoring gate.

`Size/model suggestion:` M.

PR #17524 carried it correctly from the start; the missing half was mine. Completing it here so the two carriers agree in substance, not only in the fixed spelling.

That exact string is in **neither** file — it blends `validating-metadata.mdx:580` with `cli.mdx:1385`. Both are genuinely published and the substance is exactly right, so this is ⛔ not a defect in the declaration; the three lines above are the byte-exact form, and this comment is the carrier that holds them.

**Why `no` and not `yes`:** all three published lines state that the three authoring doors judge one stack. `os validate` and `os lint` were not doing that. Making them do it **narrows** what they accept, back onto text that was already published — 「拉回已声明契约不触它」 (`SKILL.md`) and 「收窄仍是语义面,不触条款②」 (`references/lanes/spec.md`).
